eyebrow: The T-SQL Development Course · Chapter Ten
subtitle: Lesson 85 · Window and Ranking Functions

code:
UNBOUNDED PRECEDING   -- start of the partition
N PRECEDING            -- N rows/values before current
CURRENT ROW            -- the current row itself
N FOLLOWING            -- N rows/values after current
UNBOUNDED FOLLOWING    -- end of the partition
caption: A frame is always BETWEEN <start> AND <end>.

code:
SELECT OrderDate, TotalDue,
  SUM(TotalDue) OVER (
    ORDER BY OrderDate
    ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW)
    AS SumOfLast3Rows
FROM Sales.SalesOrderHeader;
caption: Always exactly 3 rows — ROWS doesn't care what values they hold.

code:
SELECT OrderDate, TotalDue,
  SUM(TotalDue) OVER (
    ORDER BY OrderDate
    RANGE BETWEEN CURRENT ROW AND CURRENT ROW)
    AS SumOfRowsWithSameDate
FROM Sales.SalesOrderHeader;
caption: Every row tied on OrderDate is a PEER — all included together.

code:
-- ROWS: predictable, physical — use it almost always
-- RANGE: only when tied ORDER BY values
--         should be treated as one group
caption: This is exactly why the default LAST_VALUE frame misbehaves.
